The same declared row bundles NMDA 100 ms: Flint 1997 (rat neocortex slices, 25C, single exponential; Flint AC, Maisch US, Weishaupt JH, Kriegstein AR, Monyer H (1997) J Neurosci 17(7):2469-2476, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6573498 (opened)) gives NMDA EPSC decay 'The mean decay of NMDAR EPSCs evoked at P3/4 (262.8 ± 20.8 msec' and 'P8/9 (146 ± 9.1 msec', i.e. LONGER than the declared 100 ms in early life. Secondary compilation only (compneuro.uwaterloo.ca constants page, not primary): rat endbulb AMPA decay 1.33 ms evoked P4-11 (Bellingham 1998; primary abstract opened via Europe PMC, no AMPA tau in abstract). Hestrin 1992, Carmignoto & Vicini 1992, Burgard & Hablitz 1993 abstracts opened via Europe PMC: qualitative only (NMDA EPSC longer in young), no tau numbers in the abstracts; full texts 403/paywalled. Searches: WebSearch x4, Europe PMC x5, WebFetch x6.

row.note: Face row of SURFACES7 (onset 9.0 wk). WORLD_V7_DESIGN 7.3 tags it [V].
row.quote: 'Innervation density is not uniform across the face: we estimate an innervation density of 48 units/cm2 for the forehead, eyes, and nose (V1); 67 units/cm2 for the central part of the face (V2); and 84 units/cm2 for the lower lip, the chin, the jaw, and an area around the ears (V3). Locally, some regions such as the area immediately surrounding the mouth and the lips are likely to exhibit much higher innervation densities.' Table 1: Face V2 14,676 afferents, 67 units/cm2, 219 cm2; Face V3 16,820, 84, 200 cm2
row.source: Corniani G, Saal HP. Tactile innervation densities across the whole body. J Neurophysiol 2020;124(4):1229-1240, doi 10.1152/jn.00313.2020 (published version opened: https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/166148/8/jn.00313.2020.pdf)
row.species_age: young adult human (estimates from fibre counts and skin areas)
row.transfer: adult density -> fetal face chart. skin7's DENSITY RULE uses the adult density only as a RELATIVE weight (gain vs D_REF); a fixed afferent count over smaller fetal skin means a higher absolute fetal density, not modelled. The source warns the perioral region is likely much denser than the V2/V3 means.

row.note: MATERIAL MISMATCH (about 3x short). Sample: 'CS18〜23のヒト胚18例と、CRL 38.7〜225 mmのヒト胎児11例'. Takakuwa 2023 (full text): 'the angle in the upper limbs was relatively constant (45° to 90°)'; 'a decrease in abduction was observed in both upper and lower limbs'.

data.matches_declared: ratio ours/source 20 ms / 42-125 ms = 0.16-0.48 (0.28 at the geometric means); VERIFIER MISMATCH: NOT CONFIRMED (UNCERTAIN): the 42-125 ms scale pairs the ends of two UNPAIRED ranges. Using the amplitude threshold the model's F_FA is built from (Johansson & Vallbo 1979 RA median 13.8 um) with Knibestol's geometric-mean velocity threshold (3.96 mm/s) gives ~3.5 ms, i.e. the model (20 ms) would be ~6x MORE sensitive to slow ramps, the opposite direction. Earlier note: ARM_REST nominal internal rotation 70 (18.9 range 40-100). MATERIAL MISMATCH against the embryonic values; no fetal central value to compare. CAVEATS: (1) full text not opened, values are the authors' approximate ('約') summary figures read off their plots; (2) angle convention: Kumano measure the humerus against the trunk (body) axis with landmarks (glenoid centre, humeral condyles, T1, T5); body7 sh_flex / sh_abd / sh_rot are joint angles from the arm-down neutral of the v7 chain; the conventions were not checked against the paper's methods; (3) ex vivo specimens (post-mortem posture). GA 9.0 = 49 d PC = CS20; GA 10.0 = 56 d PC = CS23 (O'Rahilly). | VERIFIER MISMATCH (round 4, value NOT changed; finding in DECISIONS_PENDING): UNCERTAIN: -10..+10 deg embryonic values verified, but the rotation reference (zero position, landmark axis) is not stated in any accessible text, so the 30-80 deg gap cannot be confirmed without the Kumano full text (Wiley 403).

data.name: note
data.value: Kumano amendment v1.1 SHOULD-2 (declared approximation): the GA 18 abduction nominal 23.0 deg uses the INTERGROWTH CRL dating EXTRAPOLATED beyond ~95 mm for the middle-fetal groups; the paper's own ~13-22 wk would give 15.6 deg (two-sided: fixation shrinkage biases the other way). Read any GA 18 residual / SRC_CONFLICT against this band. Earlier note: Shoulder abduction at rest, GA 18 (ARM_REST_TAB col 2; negative = adduction across the chest, LIMITS sh_abd -45..120). Ours is DERIVED (w7_build/recentre.py, WORLD_V7_DESIGN 18.11 R-ARM: nearest overlap-free hands-together posture to the 18.9 nominal). Mismatch likely early in the fetal period (11.5-14 wk), small by mid-fetal; not quantifiable from the summary. CAVEATS: (1) full text not opened, values are the authors' approximate ('約') summary figures read off their plots; (2) angle convention: Kumano measure the humerus against the trunk (body) axis with landmarks (glenoid centre, humeral condyles, T1, T5); body7 sh_flex / sh_abd / sh_rot are joint angles from the arm-down neutral of the v7 chain; the conventions were not checked against the paper's methods; (3) ex vivo specimens (post-mortem posture). GA 9.0 = 49 d PC = CS20; GA 10.0 = 56 d PC = CS23 (O'Rahilly). | VERIFIER MISMATCH (round 4, value NOT changed; finding in DECISIONS_PENDING): UNCERTAIN magnitude: ours -10 (projected ~-11.5) vs a value declining from ~+70 toward 0 by mid-fetal; no per-GA source value; sign mismatch likely at 11.5-14 wk, small by 18 wk.

data.quote: Text: 'Overall, 7 VPM units were isolated from 3- to 6-day-old rats'; 'exhibited a significant increase in firing rate 100 ms after a twitch, peaking at approximately 250 ms'; 'all recording was performed in unanesthetized subjects'. Fig. 3 legend: '(C) Perievent histogram for the VPM unit' (y axis 'Firing rate (Hz)', ticks 0.0 / 1.6 / 3.2); '(E) VPM unit firing rate (spikes/5 s), unit activity, and bursts activity over a 15-min recording session.' No time-mean rate is stated in the text; the value is read from the figure.
data.species_age: rat (Sprague-Dawley), P3-P6, head-fixed, unanesthetized, natural sleep-wake cycling with whisker twitches (spontaneous + self-generated-movement reafference)
data.transfer: declared: species rat -> human; locus VPM (lemniscal relay one synapse downstream of PrV barrelette neurons) -> PrV/SpV principal neurons; age rat P3-P6 (PC day 24-27) -> by Workman et al. 2013 (J Neurosci 33:7368, PMC3928428; Table 2: rat ln(PC day) = 2.31 + 1.705*X, human 3.167 + 3.72*X, no interaction term for non-cortical events) human PC about 158-204 d = about 24-31 wk GA (LMP), whereas the target 9.0-14.0 wk GA (PC 49-84 d) maps to rat about E14-E18 (first PrV postsynaptic responses at E15, Waite et al. 2000 Eur J Neurosci 12:2781); state unanesthetized sleep/wake -> in-utero ongoing activity
data.value_in_source: about 1 imp/s (figure-read, one representative VPM unit): Fig. 3C pre-twitch bins 0.4-1.6 Hz (mean about 0.9 Hz), twitch-evoked peak about 3.2 Hz; Fig. 3E 15-min trace 0 to about 17 spikes/5 s in active sleep (0-3.4 Hz), near 0 in wake, i.e. a session time mean of roughly 0.5-1 imp/s

Text: "Overall, 7 VPM units were isolated from 3- to 6-day-old rats (n=7)"; "exhibited a significant increase in firing rate 100 ms after a twitch, peaking at approximately 250 ms"; "all recording was performed in unanesthetized subjects" (surgery under isoflurane). data.value: RESEARCHED AS core_v0.rho (0.05); RE-KEYED by the designer to the future cid tg.rho_tg (RHO_TG = 0.005 in tg.py, M0 v1.5 16.3, D-M0R-15): the source does not support 0.05. Implied RHO = 1 / 200 = 0.005 (range from the figure 0.5-1.6 Hz -> 0.0025-0.008). This is 10x below the current frozen 0.05 (10 imp/s) and 2x above the corrected cortex 0.0025 (0.5 imp/s). The age transfer runs toward a LOWER rate (target is ~2 rat-weeks earlier, at the onset of trigeminal-nucleus synaptic transmission), so 0.005 is best read as an upper-side estimate; 0.05 is not supported by any neonatal relay data found. Recommendation: TG RHO = 0.005 declared transfer; sensitivity 0.0025-0.01. Weakness: figure-read value from one representative unit, not a stated population mean; no PrV/SpV in-vivo developmental unit rates exist in the literature searched.
